title: Fibonacci Diagonal Sum Identity via Binomial Coefficients

problemStatement.plain: The sum of binomial coefficients along the "diagonal" of Pascal's triangle — specifically the terms $\binom{n}{0} + \binom{n-1}{1} + \binom{n-2}{2} + \cdots$ — equals the $(n+1)$-th Fibonacci number. Prove this by induction using the Fibonacci recurrence $F(n+2)=F(n+1)+F(n)$ and Pascal's rule $\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n-1}{k} + \binom{n-1}{k-1}$.
